item.title: Hermitian connections and holonomy with parallel torsions
item.description: arXiv:2611.28243v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $(M^n,g,J)$ be a connected Hermitian manifold of complex dimension $n\geq2$, and let $\nabla$ be a Hermitian connection with nonzero parallel torsion. Assuming that its restricted holonomy acts irreducibly on $T^{1,0}M$, the author proved that the first Ricci curvature must vanish. In this paper we derive a Berger like complete list of its holonomy representations: the complexified adjoint representation of a compact simple Lie algebra, and the standard seven-dimensional complex representation of compact $\Gtwo$. Curvature of such a connection is proven to be parallel. Secondly, without irreducibility assumption, we derive an explicit local normal form for the metric whose Chern connection has parallel trosion, which includes holomorphic warpings and nontrivial holomorphic extensions of hyperk\"ahler manifolds. For complete metrics with bounded Chern curvature, the characters associated with nontrivial global restricted-holonomy blocks vanish. Compact metrics admit an unwarped local form, are balanced, and have a unimodular vertical Lie algebra. On their universal covers, suitable K\"ahler factors split off and the remaining factor has vanishing first Chern Ricci form. A compact simply connected elliptic bundle over a K3 surface explains why this local classification does not give a global product classification. This extends the classification result of Zheng and author on Hermitian manifolds whose Chern connection is Ambrose-Singer. In particular, the analysis shows that if the metric is not K\"ahler its Chern curvature must satisfies $\Rm_{(\cdot), (\cdot)}X=0$ for some parallel nonzero vector $X\in T'M$. In appendix we include a by-product: On a compact complex homogenous space $M$ with finite fundamental group, any Hermitian metric whose Chern connection has parallel torsion, must be K\"ahler.
item.dc:creator: Lei Ni

item.title: Topology-Preserving Hodge--Laplacian Diffusion on Manifolds with Boundary
item.description: arXiv:2611.28363v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Overview: We study deterministic and stochastic Hodge--Laplacian diffusion of differential forms on a fixed smooth compact Riemannian manifold with boundary. Absolute and relative boundary conditions select harmonic spaces representing ordinary and relative cohomology. We investigate the preservation properties of these diffusion processes, their compatible cellular discretizations, and their implications for reverse diffusion models. Numerical experiments on an annulus and a solid torus illustrate the theoretical results. Mathematical Significance: Using the de Rham complex and its constant-sheaf interpretation, we distinguish preservation of harmonic coordinates from preservation of a cohomology class. We establish that deterministic heat flow preserves the harmonic projection and exponentially damps its orthogonal complement. For additive stochastic forcing, we prove that pathwise harmonic preservation is equivalent to the absence of harmonic noise. Exact forcing preserves closedness and the initial cohomology class for closed initial data, whereas harmonic-projected forcing need not preserve closedness. We further show that compatible cellular discretizations retain these properties, with an algebraic extension to fixed weighted cellular sheaves. Separating invariant preservation from time-step stability and covariance accuracy, we derive bounds on leakage arising from approximate harmonic projectors. AI Relevance: We develop a finite-dimensional conditional score formulation that confines reverse diffusion to a prescribed harmonic component or, for closed data, a fixed cohomology class. This provides a mathematically grounded framework for incorporating topological constraints into diffusion-based generative AI models on manifolds.
item.dc:creator: Chen-Chih Lai, Sean Cottrell, Guo-Wei Wei

item.title: An Isoperimetric Comparison for a Variational Threshold Associated with the Riemannian \(p\)-Laplacian
item.description: arXiv:2611.28410v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a variational threshold $\Lambda_{p,M}(K)$ associated with a one-phase free boundary functional involving the Riemannian $p$-Dirichlet energy and a volume penalization on a bounded domain $K$ of a Riemannian manifold $M$. In the Euclidean case, this threshold is the smallest parameter for which the interior Bernoulli problem has a solution minimizing the energy; it bounds the Bernoulli constant from above, and the inequality is strict for balls. We characterize $\Lambda_{p,M}(K)$ as the infimum of a capacity-to-volume quotient and prove that this infimum is always attained. We then prove an isoperimetric comparison theorem: domination of the isoperimetric profile of $M$ by that of a model space implies a lower bound for $\Lambda_{p,M}(K)$ in terms of the threshold of a model geodesic ball. This extends a theorem of Daners and Kawohl. For geodesic balls in space forms, we give an explicit one-dimensional formula for the threshold and prove its strict monotonicity in the curvature, at fixed radius and at fixed volume. As applications, we obtain comparison results on compact manifolds with positive Ricci curvature, through the normalized L\'evy--Gromov inequality, and on manifolds with nonnegative Ricci curvature and Euclidean volume growth, where the factor $\mbox{AVR}^{1/N}$ appears; a product-cylinder example shows that nonnegative Ricci curvature alone is not sufficient. Finally, we characterize the equality cases: geodesic balls in space forms, round spheres and geodesic balls in the L\'evy--Gromov setting, Euclidean space and balls in the setting of Euclidean volume growth.
item.dc:creator: Ababacar Sadikhe Djit\'e, Diaraf Seck

item.title: On p-Group Actions and Index Divisibilities
item.description: arXiv:2611.28449v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a mod-$ p $ divisibility result for indices of elliptic operators assuming a smooth action by a finite $ p $-group on the base manifold of dimension $ n\le 2(p-1) $ with no stationary points and which lifts equivariantly to the operator bundles. We show as one consequence that if such manifolds are spin or stably almost complex, with the group action lifting to the relevant structure, then their class in the relevant bordism theory modulo $ p $ is fully determined by one genus, and indeed vanishes for $ n<2(p-1) $. We show as another consequence that there exists no closed connected $ 24 $-dimensional spin manifold $ M $ satisfying $ {\hat{A}(M)=1}, {\hat{A}(M;T_\mathbb{C}M)=0} $, and for which there exists a smooth non-trivial action by the monster group, resolving a question of Hirzebruch.
item.dc:creator: Kyle Gettig

item.title: Superintegrable Systems and the Tractor Connection
item.description: arXiv:2611.28568v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quadratic constants of motion for natural pseudo-Riemannian Hamiltonians with potential correspond to conformal Killing tensors admitting multiple Killing scales. Taking this correspondence further, we develop a dimension-independent ($n\ge 3$) framework for studying second-order superintegrable systems using conformal tractor calculus, and invariant BGG prolongation of the rank two conformal Killing equation. We apply this framework to classify second-order maximally superintegrable systems within certain natural families of Hamiltonians generated by pairs of conformally related Einstein metrics in arbitrary dimensions. We recover the second-order analogue of Bertrand's theorem as a special case.
item.dc:creator: Simon C. W. Goodwin, A. Rod Gover, Jonathan M. Kress

item.title: The Space of $k$-Positive Potentials
item.description: arXiv:2611.28679v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study weak geodesics in the space of $k$-positive potentials on a compact K\"ahler manifold. We prove that any two smooth strictly $k$-positive potentials can be joined by a weak geodesic of class $C^{1,1}$. As an application, we prove that the pair $(\mathcal H_k,d_2)$ is a metric space.
item.dc:creator: XiShen Jin

item.title: On a simple family of Ricci-flows of O(3)-hypersurfaces: Counterexamples to the theorem on the preservation of positive definite Ricci curvature everywhere
item.description: arXiv:2611.28739v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This note provides a concise derivation of the equation of Ricci \'aows on O(n)-rotational hypersurfaces in En+1 which consists of a pair of parabolic equations (cf. Lemma 2 of {\ss}4) via simple applications of classical theorems of rotational surfaces in E3, governing the Ricci-evolution of their generating plane curves. Furthermore, the second equation can be transformed to that of the evolution equation of their "curvature pro\"Oles" (cf. Lemmas 3 and 3\'iof {\ss}4). In {\ss}5, we consider a speci\"Oc family of initial generating curves of "curvature pro\"Oles" that are only tiny modi\"Ocations of the constant function K= 1 R ;R 1, in a very small vicinity of the symmetric middle point as indicated in Fig. 2. Note that the short-time unique existence of analytic solutions of such a simple system of parabolic equations follows simply via Nash-Moser Theory. The simple estimate of {\ss}5 shows the curvature k1( t(0)) is already becoming negative at a very short time (cf. {\ss}5.3).
item.dc:creator: Wu-Chung Hsiang, Wu-Yi Hsiang

item.title: Normal Homogeneous Counterexamples to Wolf's Homogeneity Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2611.28771v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct free Clifford--Wolf subgroups of order two whose quotients of compact, connected, simply connected normal homogeneous manifolds are not homogeneous. The universal covers are the oriented real flag manifolds $M_{d}=SO(N)/\prod_{i=1}^{q}SO(d_{i})$, equipped with the metric induced by the negative Killing form, where $N\geq4$ and $q\geq3$ is odd. We determine its full connected centralizer, the effective connected isometry group of the quotient, and the corresponding orbit space. These calculations prove nonhomogeneity and give explicit formulas for the cohomogeneity, fundamental group, and Euler characteristic. These examples are found by ChatGPT 6 Astra.
item.dc:creator: Zaili Yan, Hui Zhang

item.title: Finite-Time Singularities of the $L_\beta$-Gradient Flow in a K\"ahler Surface
item.description: arXiv:2611.28821v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study finite-time singularities of the $L_\beta$-gradient flow of closed symplectic surfaces in a compact K\"ahler surface, with $\beta > 0$ fixed. We derive the evolution equation for the second fundamental form and obtain a lower bound on the blow-up rate of its maximum squared norm. Combining this bound with a local curvature propagation estimate and the weighted monotonicity formula, we rule out Type I singularities.
item.dc:creator: Weihan Wang

item.title: On Partially Totally Real Riemannian Maps and Their Sharp Curvature Inequalities
item.description: arXiv:2611.28886v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce partially totally real Riemannian maps into K\"ahler manifolds and examine the geometry of their associated distributions. For complex space forms, we obtain a Chen-type curvature inequality retaining the contributions of the mixed second fundamental form and O'Neill's tensor, together with an arbitrary-codimension estimate involving partial mean curvatures. We characterize equality in the principal inequality and give an example attaining the bound when $\dim\mathcal D\geq4$, including a case with nonintegrable horizontal distribution.
item.dc:creator: Tanveer Fatima

item.title: Killing Scales for Conformal Killing Tensors of Rank Two and Higher
item.description: arXiv:2611.29124v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study which metrics in a conformal class admit a Killing tensor with prescribed conformal Killing trace-free part. We call such metrics Killing scales. We also consider whether a given conformal Killing tensor is itself a Killing tensor for some metric in the conformal class, as well as the analogous problem for conformal Killing-Yano forms. Our approach to this problem uses conformal and projective tractors, and the prolongations provided by the BGG splitting operators of the projective and conformal Killing operators. For rank two conformal Killing tensors, we characterise local Killing scales for arbitrary scales on arbitrary conformal manifolds, extending recent results that were restricted to Einstein scales on conformally flat manifolds. The criterion is expressed in terms of the scale tractor and the BGG prolongation of the conformal Killing tensor. We also obtain Killing scale criteria for higher-rank conformal Killing tensors and conformal Killing-Yano forms, under additional hypotheses involving Einstein scales and normal solutions. We describe the tractor geometry of special Einstein products, including Ricci-flat products, and use these constructions to give examples beyond the conformally flat setting.
item.dc:creator: Simon C. W. Goodwin, A. Rod Gover, Thomas Leistner

item.title: Counterexamples to the $k$-harmonic conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2611.29160v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct nonminimal $k$-harmonic hypersurfaces in $\R^{n+1}$ for every $k\geq3$ and $n\geq3$, giving counterexamples to the $k$-harmonic conjecture. Each example has exact order $k$ and is an incomplete circular cone or a Euclidean product of such a cone. We also classify the $k$-harmonic circular cones, determine the possible dimensions of nonminimal cones with closed links, and give constructions in higher codimension.
item.dc:creator: Yu Fu, Yanru Luo, Dan Yang

item.title: Cylindrical Ricci flows and the PDE-ODI principle
item.description: arXiv:2611.29246v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We derive precise asymptotics for ancient asymptotically cylindrical Ricci flows. We establish a dichotomy in which the leading deviation from the cylinder is either linear or quadratic in the axial variables. In the linear case, we show that the flow is exponentially asymptotic to a Bryant soliton times a Euclidean factor. For $\kappa$-solutions, we further show that the flow is isometric to such a product, up to parabolic rescaling. In the quadratic case, we obtain higher-order asymptotics governed by a finite-dimensional invariant. We also establish propagation of cylindrical regions and uniqueness of cylindrical tangent flows. These results closely parallel those in our earlier work on cylindrical mean curvature flows. Both analyses use the same PDE-ODI principle and yield a unified treatment of cylindrical Ricci flow and mean curvature flow. The essential new ingredient in the Ricci flow setting is a coherent harmonic map heat flow gauge, which allows us to apply this principle without assuming a sign for the curvature. The local analytic tools developed here also form part of a program aimed at constructing Ricci flow with surgery in dimension 4.
item.dc:creator: Richard H. Bamler, Yi Lai

item.title: Five-dimensional homogeneous Riemannian manifolds with harmonic curvature are Ricci-parallel
item.description: arXiv:2611.29373v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we show that 5-dimensional homogeneous Riemannian manifolds with harmonic curvature are Ricci-parallel.
item.dc:creator: Charif Bourzik, Othmane Dani, Mehdi Nabil

item.title: Fixed-Time Heat Kernel Integrals on Flat Tori: a Finer Invariantthan the Heat Trace
item.description: arXiv:2611.29403v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let \[T^n = \mathbb{R}^n/\Lambda\] be a flat torus and let \[k_t\]be its heat kernel. For a primitive lattice vector \[\lambda_0 \in \Lambda\] let \[ \gamma_{\lambda_0}(s) = s\lambda_0/|\lambda_0|, \qquad s \in [0, |\lambda_0|], \] and \[ I_t(\lambda_0) = \int_{0}^{|\lambda_0|} k_t(0, \gamma_{\lambda_0}(s)) \, ds. \] The integral \[I_t(\lambda_0)\] combines spectral data (the heat kernel) with geometric data (a choice of closed geodesic), and is a strictly finer invariant than the heat trace \[ K_t = \int_{T^n} k_t(x, x) \, dx. \] We prove the following. (i) For n = 1, \[I_t(\lambda_0) = 1\] for every t > 0 and every primitive \[\lambda_0\]; the fixed-time data carry no geometric information. (ii) For n = 2, for any fixed t_0 > 0 the multiset \[ \mathcal{D}_{t_0} = \{I_{t_0}(\lambda_0) : \lambda_0 \text{ primitive}\}/\{\pm\} \] determines \(\Lambda\) up to isometry, and hence the length spectrum, the volume, and the isometry class of T^2. (iii) For n = 16, the fixed-time data distinguish Milnor's isospectral non-isometric tori \[ \mathbb{R}^{16}/(D_8^+ \times D_8^+) \quad \text{and} \quad \mathbb{R}^{16}/D_{16}^+ \] for all \[t_0 > 0\] outside a countable set, although their heat traces agree at every t > 0.
item.dc:creator: Hossein Mohades

item.title: Prescribing finite first singular sets of mean curvature flow in $\mathbb{R}^3$
item.description: arXiv:2611.29429v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For any $n$ distinct points in $\mathbb{R}^3$ and any sufficiently small positive time, we construct a smooth mean curvature flow of embedded mean-convex tori whose first singularities occur precisely at those points at that time.
item.dc:creator: Jingwen Chen

item.title: A sharp conjugate radius bound for open four-manifolds with positive bi-Ricci curvature
item.description: arXiv:2611.29593v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that every complete noncompact Riemannian four-manifold without boundary with bi-Ricci curvature at least $b>0$ has conjugate radius at most $\pi\sqrt{2/b}$. Equality holds on the round cylinder $\bS^3(\sqrt{2/b})\times\bR$. For $b=2$, the bound and the equality model agree with Gromov's prediction for open four-manifolds under a scalar curvature lower bound of $6$.
item.dc:creator: Ronggang LI

item.title: Support functions of sections of $p$-minimal tubes
item.description: arXiv:2611.29625v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $M$ be a compact $p$-minimal hypersurface in ${\mathbb R}^{n+1}$ with boundary in two parallel hyperplanes. We study the convex hulls $\Omega(\tau)$ of its horizontal sections through their support function $H(\tau,\cdot)$, without any assumption on the topology of $M$. We prove that $H$ is a viscosity subsolution of a degenerate elliptic inequality. For $n=2$ it is of Monge--Amp\`ere type, and its equality case for minimal surfaces with circular sections is Riemann's system. A posteriori, $H$ is locally semiconvex and every hull is a smooth convex body; the inequality then also holds in the sense of measures, with the edges of the hulls appearing as atoms of Alexandrov's area functions. Averaging over directions gives a catenary-type inequality for the mean width of the hulls. It yields lifetime bounds for $p$-minimal tubes when $n>p$. For minimal surfaces in ${\mathbb R}^3$ it gives a sharp bound for the distance between the planes in terms of the perimeters of the hulls of the boundary curves, with equality only for a catenoid. For one convex curve in each plane this recovers, by a different method, the nonexistence and rigidity theorem of Bernstein and Breiner. The bound extends to non-convex curves and to boundaries with several components. Finally, we show that the Meeks annulus conjecture is equivalent to the absence of atoms in the area functions of the hulls of all intermediate sections.
item.dc:creator: Vladimir G. Tkachev

item.title: $p$-Harmonic gauge and the regularity of spacetime isometries
item.description: arXiv:2611.29643v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show every Lorentzian metric of class $C^{k,\alpha}$, where $k\in\mathbf{N}_0$ and $\alpha\in(0,1)$, admits local coordinates of class $C^{k+1,\alpha}$ all of whose coordinate functions are temporal functions that are harmonic with respect to a nonlinear $p$-wave operator, where $p\in(-\infty,1)$. Unlike the classical wave operator, this operator is elliptic on temporal functions. As an application, we show that an isometry between Lorentzian metrics of class $C^{k,\alpha}$ is of class $C^{k+1,\alpha}$.
item.dc:creator: Mathias Braun

item.title: Inverse spectra and Wilson traces of $SU(2)$ connections on finite graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.29644v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a fixed $SU(2)$ connection on a known finite labelled simple graph through its full Laplacian spectra with independently variable positive edge weights. This family is equivalent to all vertex-simple cycle traces. For connected graphs, it determines every vertex gauge class exactly for trees and graphs with a single cyclic block that is a cycle, a theta graph, or a subdivision of a simple three-vertex-connected cubic graph. For arbitrary graphs, we describe the full fibers, including degenerate connections, and give criteria for generic uniqueness and Wilson observability under restricted edge controls.
item.dc:creator: Haoxuan Cheng

item.title: Superpotentials for F-manifolds and bi-flat F-structures on the orbit spaces of reflection groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.29736v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We extend Dubrovin's construction of a superpotential from Frobenius manifolds to biflat F-manifolds. The key step in this extension is choosing a flat coordinate of one of the connections studied in [11] and invert this coordinate with respect to the spectral parameter and the construction does not require an invariant metric. Suppose that the manifold has dimension n and that the superpotential admits a holomorphic continuation to n simple critical points with distinct critical values. These values give canonical coordinates, and the residue formulas recover both the product and the flat connection from the superpotential alone. Conversely, under suitable nondegeneracy conditions, a solution of the superpotential equations for a given product defines a biflat F-manifold. For $B_n$ and $G(m,1,n)$ we obtain the whole family of biflat structures from a polynomial superpotential by varying a twisted primary differential. For $G(m,m,n)$ we obtain the natural biflat structure from a Laurent superpotential. Keeping the Laurent polynomial fixed and varying the primary differential gives a new family of flat F-manifolds depending on one parameter. We use the superpotential and the poles of the dual product along the reflecting hyperplanes to prove the conjecture we formulated in [8] for irreducible Coxeter groups and in [10] for well generated complex reflection groups. The conjecture concerns biflat F-structures whose dual connection has the form studied by Dunkl and Kohno. When the reflecting hyperplanes form a single orbit, we identify the biflat structure associated with the flat structure of [24,25,27]. We obtain the remaining families from the polynomial construction for $G(m,1,n)$ and an explicit computation for $F_4$. In every case the first flat structure extends polynomially to the whole quotient, and the biflat structure is defined on the complement of the reflection discriminant.
item.dc:creator: Alessandro Arsie, Paolo Lorenzoni

item.title: A compact nonformal manifold with holonomy Spin(7)
item.description: arXiv:2611.29751v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct a compact simply connected eight-manifold with holonomy Spin(7) and a triple Massey product of degrees $(3,2,2)$ that does not contain zero. The manifold is a resolution of a flat orbifold. Joyce's gluing theorem gives it a torsion-free Spin(7) structure. The resolution map factors through a quotient of $Y\times S^1$, where $Y$ is Mart\'in-Merch\'an's nonformal $G_2$ manifold. The map to this quotient has degree one, so pullback preserves a nonzero Massey pairing. On the resolution the detecting degree-two class annihilates the full indeterminacy. Simple connectivity and nonformality imply full Spin(7) holonomy. The manifold has $(b_2,b_3,b_4^+,b_4^-)=(22,10,91,27)$.
item.dc:creator: Yaroslav Bazaikin

item.title: Simple closed geodesics on the Klein bottle: the sharp lower bound
item.description: arXiv:2611.29810v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We revisit the Klein bottle case of Ballmann's theorem on simple closed geodesics. The final counting argument in Ballmann's proof relies on the existence of a nontrivial homological family in a primitive one-sided free homotopy class. We identify an obstruction to this assertion and establish instead the lower bound of four geometrically distinct simple closed geodesics: two in the horizontal two-sided class and one in each of the two primitive one-sided classes. We then show that this bound is sharp. The exclusion of any additional simple closed geodesics is obtained by combining the topology of the orientation double cover with a separation of the geodesic equations and a period estimate based on Wirtinger's inequality.
item.dc:creator: Gabriella Freitas, Marcelo Miranda

item.title: Sharp integral Ricci pinching on manifolds with positive total scalar curvature
item.description: arXiv:2611.29866v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $(M,g)$ be a closed connected Riemannian three-manifold with $\int_M R \mathrm{d}v>0$, and assume that $M$ is not diffeomorphic to a spherical space form. We prove the sharp integral Ricci pinching inequality $$\mathrm{vol}(g)\int_M |\mathrm{Ric}^{\circ}|^2 \mathrm{d}v \geq \frac{1}{6}\left(\int_M R \mathrm{d}v\right)^2.$$ Moreover, equality holds if and only if $(M,g)$ is locally isometric to $\mathbb{S}^2(a)\times\mathbb{R}$ for some $a>0$. By the same method, we prove $\mathrm{vol}(g)\int_M |\mathrm{Ric}^{\circ}|^2 \mathrm{d}v \geq \frac{1}{12}\left(\int_M R \mathrm{d}v\right)^2$ on closed four-manifolds with $\int_M R \mathrm{d}v>0$ that have a finite cover with positive first Betti number, and we provide a new proof of Gursky's inequality. We also show that the corresponding inequality fails in every dimension $n\geq 5$, and we give a metric on $\mathbb{S}^2\times\mathbb{S}^1$ that disproves a conjecture of Ge, Li and Lian.
item.dc:creator: Guofang Wang, Wei Wei

item.title: Logarithmic Potential and its Applications in Conformal Geometry
item.description:
arXiv:2611.29887v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish an intrinsic characterization of the end invariants $
u_i$ in the Chern--Gauss--Bonnet formula for complete, simply connected, locally conformally flat 4-manifolds with non-negative scalar curvature and $Q$-curvature non-negative outside a compact set. For each end $M_i$, we show that $
u_i$ is the cube root of its normalized asymptotic geodesic-ball volume growth: \[ 
u_i=\left(\lim_{r	o\infty}  rac{V_g(B_r(p)\cap M_i)}{(\pi^2/2)r^4}ight)^{1/3}. \] This characterization uses only the Riemannian distance and volume of $g$; it is independent of the base point $p$, the choice of compact truncation of the end, and any conformal coordinates. The proof is based on asymptotic radial symmetry of the logarithmic potential outside a sparse $\mathscr{E}$-set, inspired by Hayman's work \cite{hayman1960slowly}, together with comparisons of radial lengths and geodesic distances.
item.dc:creator: Liming Liu, Shiguang Ma

item.title: On the moduli space of nonpositively curved metrics on a product with a torus
item.description: arXiv:2611.29892v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that if $N$ is a closed smooth manifold admitting a Riemannian metric of negative sectional curvature and $T^k$ is the $k$-dimensional torus, then there is a retraction from the moduli space of nonpositively curved Riemannian metrics on $T^k\times N$ onto the moduli space of flat metrics on $T^k$. As an application, we combine our retraction with Tuschmann and Wiemeler's work on the rational topology of the moduli space of flat metrics on $T^k$ to deduce that the moduli space of nonpositively curved metrics on $T^k\times N$ has nontrivial higher rational homotopy and cohomology groups when $k\geq5$.
item.dc:creator: F. Thomas Farrell, Yi Jiang

item.title: Singularities of Mean Curvature Flow with Bounded Total Curvature II: Multiplicity One
item.description: arXiv:2611.29956v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let \(M_t^n\subset\mathbb R^{n+1}\) be a smooth mean curvature flow of closed embedded hypersurfaces, with \(n\ge3\), and let \(T\) be its first singular time. If the integral of \(|A|^n\) is uniformly bounded for \(t<T\), every nonzero tangent flow at time \(T\) has multiplicity one. At each singular point the tangent flow is unique, and the rescaled flow converges locally smoothly to a closed self-shrinker.
item.dc:creator: Yongheng Han, Zhen Wang

item.title: Self-similar solutions to the inverse mean curvature flow in the Lorentz--Minkowski plane
item.description: arXiv:2611.29979v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We classify the self-similar solutions of the inverse mean curvature flow in the Lorentz--Minkowski plane $\mathbb{R}^{1,1}$. Using hyperbolic numbers, the self-similarity condition becomes a linear ODE system, and all solutions are obtained in closed form with explicit smoothness and completeness criteria. Translating solitons occur in three causal types, and dilation--rotation solitons are governed by the discriminant $\Delta=a^2-4(b-1)$, as in the Euclidean case. When $a^2=b^2$ the translation cannot be eliminated, owing to the zero divisors of the hyperbolic numbers, and a genuinely Lorentzian class of mixed solitons arises, whose complete smooth members form a one-parameter family. The planar classification is then extended to translationally invariant solutions in $\mathbb{R}^{n,1}$, and rotationally invariant solutions are reduced to an explicit ODE system.
item.dc:creator: Li Ou

item.title: Obstructed Harvey--Lawson cones and logarithmic special Lagrangian singularities
item.description: arXiv:2611.30082v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct two exact embedded special Lagrangian germs with the same unique multiplicity-one tangent cone, the Harvey--Lawson cone in $\mathbb C^9$. A quadratic obstruction and a corrected cubic obstruction yield the distinct sharp $C^1$ convergence rates $\lvert\log r\rvert^{-1}$ and $\lvert\log r\rvert^{-1/2}$, respectively. These rates distinguish the germs under unitary transformations and dilations. We also prove Jacobi nonintegrability of the Harvey--Lawson cones in $\mathbb C^8$ and $\mathbb C^9$, and realize the sharp rate $\lvert\log r\rvert^{-1/2}$ at the eight-dimensional cone.
item.dc:creator: Wei-Chun Chen, Chun-Kai Lien

item.title: Difference estimates for Chern connections on homolomorphic vector bundles
item.description: arXiv:2611.30103v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates the uniqueness issue of Chern connections from the Cheng-Yau type estimate point of view. We establish local difference estimates for Chern connections on holomorphic vector bundles over complete noncompact K\"{a}hler manifolds with Ricci curvature bounded from below. These local estimates not only enable us to obtain uniqueness results for Hermitian-Einstein connections on complete noncompact K\"{a}hler manifolds with nonnegative Ricci curvature, but also apply to study the Liouville theorem for complex Monge-Amp\`{e}re equation on $\mathbb{C}^n$ as well as the Chern flatness and K\"{a}hlerness for Hermitian metrics on complete noncompact Ricci flat K\"{a}hler manifolds.
item.dc:creator: Chenghong He, Di Wu, Xi Zhang

item.title: Spacelike Curve Shortening Flow of Entire Graphs in One Spacelike Codimension
item.description: arXiv:2611.30208v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study curve shortening flow of entire spacelike graphs in the pseudo-Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^{2,k}$, $k\geq1$, where the graph directions have mixed spacelike and timelike signature. Consequently, the region of spacelike slopes is nonconvex, making the preservation of spacelikeness more delicate. We identify a natural geometric condition that overcomes this difficulty: the closed convex hull of the initial slopes is compactly contained in the spacelike region. We prove that the convex hull is preserved along the flow, yielding uniform spacelikeness and uniform acausality. For initially $C^{1,\alpha}$ graphs, we establish global existence and uniqueness, without assuming convexity or initial curvature bounds. If the initial perturbation vanishes at spatial infinity, we further prove smooth and uniform convergence to the prescribed affine spacelike line, without rescaling. Finally, we show that every ancient entire graphical flow with globally bounded slopes that remains uniformly spacelike throughout its evolution is a stationary affine line.
item.dc:creator: Artemis A. Vogiatzi, Qiyu Zhou

item.title: Families of regular non-Berwald Landsberg surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.30212v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct families of smooth, strongly convex, non-Berwald Landsberg metrics of zero flag curvature on open subsets of the plane. Each metric is regular in every nonzero tangent direction and is nonreversible. The indicatrices are obtained from the inverse differential of a periodically forced oscillator. The construction is indexed by smooth balanced periodic seeds satisfying a simple characteristic condition at a nonzero initial value. It includes single-frequency seeds of every even frequency at least four, mixtures of interacting frequencies, and seed neighborhoods of arbitrarily large finite dimension within the balanced class. A normalized profile of the canonical Cartan invariant distinguishes fixed seed orbits at sufficiently small amplitudes. In particular, the construction yields countably infinitely many pairwise locally nonhomothetic metrics. The analytic problem is to make the actual return map equal to the identity on an open set of nonzero initial values. We show that exact return on a fixed open set forces three balance equations on the seed. Under a positive drift condition a finite formal approximation gives an arbitrarily high prescribed power of a small amplitude in the return error. We normalize the complete two-branch linearized operator and reduce its scalar part to a real transport direction. A local inverse, followed by an exact correction of the full vector remainder, yields estimates with a fixed loss of derivatives. A smoothing iteration then eliminates the actual return error on a fixed open set of positive radius while retaining the seed as the leading nonlinearity.
item.dc:creator: Ming Li, Kefeng Liu

item.title: Stability and bifurcation of shrinking spheres for the fractional mean curvature flow
item.description: arXiv:2611.30246v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the fractional mean curvature flow near shrinking spheres. The first shape eigenvalue changes sign at \(s_*(n)=(\sqrt{n^2+6n+1}-n-1)/2\). Above this threshold, sufficiently small perturbations of a sphere become extinct at one point, and their extinction rescalings converge exponentially to the round shrinker. Below the threshold, the sphere is nonlinearly unstable modulo translations and dilations. We also construct smooth, strictly convex, nonspherical homothetic shrinkers bifurcating from the spherical family near the threshold. In the plane, the noncircular branch bifurcates on the side \(s>s_*(2)\).
item.dc:creator: Annalisa Cesaroni, Matteo Novaga

item.title: A note on Kaluza-Klein theories
item.description: arXiv:2611.30285v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a variant of the Kaluza-Klein theory that was introduced in previous papers (ATMP, 2020; LMP 2022; Ann. Fac. Sci. Toulouse, 2025), based on an action functional whose critical points, in the presence of point-wise constraints, lead-under reasonable assumptions-to the existence of a principal fiber bundle and solutions to the Einstein-Yang-Mills system. The difference is that it is not necessary to impose a point-wise constraint.
item.dc:creator: Fr{\'e}d{\'e}ric H{\'e}lein (IMJ-PRG)

item.title: Free-boundary minimal varifolds I: zero boundary mass
item.description: arXiv:2611.30322v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $V$ be a $k$-varifold in a compact Riemannian manifold $M^n$ with smooth nonempty boundary, where $2 \le k < n$. Assume that $V$ is stationary with free boundary and almost minimizing modulo two in every sufficiently small relative annulus about each point of $M$. We prove that $V$ is integral and that the trace of the boundary second fundamental form on $T_x V$ vanishes at $\|V\|$-almost every boundary point. On all of $M$, the first variation is $\delta V = \nu\,\sigma$, where $\nu$ is the outward unit normal and $\sigma$ is a nonnegative measure on $\partial M$ singular with respect to $\|V\|$. A strict sign for the trace on all tangent $k$-planes at each boundary point forces zero boundary mass. For hypersurfaces in ambient dimensions three through seven, strict mean convexity gives smoothness and proper embeddedness. In every bounded smooth Euclidean domain $\Omega$, we obtain $\|V\|(\Omega) \ge c_{\Omega,k}\|V\|(\overline{\Omega})$ with $c_{\Omega,k} > 0$. For smooth connected free-boundary minimal submanifolds in $\overline{\Omega}$, assuming a volume bound and a common annular almost minimizing condition at a fixed scale, then their first Dirichlet eigenvalues uniformly bounded above.
item.dc:creator: Tengyao Zhang, Zhifei Zhu

item.title: Weitzenb\"ock curvature estimates in arbitrary degree and sectional-scalar curvature pinching
item.description: arXiv:2611.30479v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For each odd dimension $n\ge7$ we give an explicit constant $B_n<(n-1)/(n+2)$ such that a closed, connected, nonflat Riemannian $n$-manifold with $K_{\min}\ge B_n S_0$ is a rational homology sphere, where $S_0=\operatorname{Scal}/[n(n-1)]$. For example, $B_7=28/43<2/3$. This answers the question of Li, Matinpour, and Petersen about lowering the sectional curvature coefficient in the remaining odd dimensions. The same argument recovers their five-dimensional endpoint $B_5=10/19$. The proof starts with a four-frame inequality for two-forms. Contracting forms and averaging over hyperplanes propagates a Ricci-weighted estimate whose coefficient depends on the parity of the codimension. For an algebraic curvature tensor with nonnegative sectional curvature, we obtain lower bounds for the Weitzenb\"ock curvature endomorphism in every degree. When the dimension and degree are both even, we classify all nonzero equality pairs for the sharp bound by powers of K\"ahler forms. For three-forms the optimal coefficient in the scalar curvature bound is $1/3$ in dimensions five and six and lies between $4/9$ and $5168/11253$ in dimension seven. On the cone of strongly nonnegative curvature tensors we determine the optimal coefficient in every degree.
item.dc:creator: Shimeng Zhang

item.title: Optimal first eigenvalue estimates for positive holomorphic sectional curvature
item.description: arXiv:2611.30482v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $(M,\omega_g)$ be a compact K\"ahler manifold with holomorphic sectional curvature $\geq 2$. We prove that the first positive eigenvalue of the Laplacian $\Delta_d$ satisfies $$\lambda_1\geq 4, $$ and $\lambda_1=4$ if and only if $(M,\omega_g)$ is holomorphically isometric to $(\mathbb{P}^1,\omega_{\mathrm{FS}})$.
item.dc:creator: Jiaxuan Fan, Mingwei Wang, Xiaokui Yang

item.title: Generic Strong Regularity and the Branson--Gover Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2611.30498v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: On each closed smooth manifold of even dimension $2N\ge 4$, we prove that the Branson--Gover detour operators are strongly regular in every degree $k-1$, $1\le k<N$, on a $C^\infty$-open dense set of Riemannian metrics. Consequently, every de Rham cohomology class of positive degree below the middle dimension has a unique conformal harmonic representative for these metrics. On a connected manifold, the critical scalar GJMS operator has only constants in its kernel on an open dense set of conformal structures modulo diffeomorphisms isotopic to the identity, as conjectured by Canzani, Gover, Jakobson, and Ponge. The proof computes the principal symbol of a reduced metric Hessian that accounts for the motion of the kernel through a Green operator.
item.dc:creator: Wei-Chun Chen, Wei-Ting Kao, Chun-Kai Lien

item.title: On the quaternionic Goldberg conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2611.30608v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a quaternionic K\"ahler analogue of the Goldberg conjecture, namely: Let $(M^8,g,\Omega)$ denote a compact $8$-manifold endowed with an $\mathrm{Sp}(2)\mathrm{Sp}(1)$-structure defined by a closed $4$-form $\Omega$. If the metric $g$ is Einstein with non-negative scalar curvature then it is quaternionic K\"ahler i.e. $\Omega$ is parallel. In fact we prove a slightly stronger result allowing for the scalar curvature to be negative under a suitable pinching condition by the square norm of the intrinsic torsion.
item.dc:creator: Udhav Fowdar

item.title: Gray II, K\"ahler Nullity and Ricci Flow on Generalized Flag Manifolds with Two Isotropy Summands
item.description: arXiv:2611.30716v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate Gray's second curvature identity, K\"ahler nullity, and homogeneous Ricci flow on generalized flag manifolds with two isotropy summands. We prove that every invariant metric satisfies Gray's second identity for both invariant almost complex structures. For the non-integrable structure, the K\"ahler nullity is trivial except at a distinguished metric ratio, where it coincides with the vertical distribution of a homogeneous fibration. This distribution is integrable and has totally geodesic leaves. For the integrable structure, the K\"ahler nullity exhibits a different behavior and need not be integrable away from the K\"ahler locus. Finally, we reduce the normalized homogeneous Ricci flow to an autonomous equation for the ratio of the metric parameters. The resulting dynamics identify two invariant Einstein directions and show that the K\"ahler--Einstein direction is attracting, while the other is repelling.
item.dc:creator: Lino Grama, Ailton R. Oliveira, Francisco V. Oliveira

item.title: Symmetry breaking Poincar{\'e}--Einstein metrics and non-extendable boundary Killing fields
item.description: arXiv:2611.30754v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct Poincar{\'e}-Einstein metrics on $R^2xS^3xS^2xS^2$ which bifurcate from anti-de Sitter black holes whose horizon is the product of a B{\"o}hm metric on $S^3xS^2$ with a round $S^2$ , and which break the rotational symmetry of the $S^2$ factor while keeping their conformal infinity. Some Killing fields of the conformal infinity therefore do not extend to the bulk, although $$\pi$^1(M, $\partial$M ) = 0$. The construction rests on two results of independent interest: the Lichnerowicz eigenvalues of B{\"o}hm metrics on invariant transverse traceless tensors are simple (with at most two exceptional values), the lowest one tends to $-$\infty$$ along B{\"o}hm's sequence with a gap to the next one tending to infinity; and large anti-de Sitter black holes in dimension nine with an Einstein horizon have no static $L^2$ perturbation of scalar type, which we prove with an explicit positive supersolution of the Kodama-Ishibashi master equation.
item.dc:creator: Erwann Delay (LMA, AU)

item.title: Normalized Weyl Energy and the Differential Topology of Four-Manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2611.30761v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Weyl functional $\int_M\|W_g\|^2\,d\mu_g$ plays an important role in four dimensional conformal geometry. Using this functional, Chang, Gursky, and Zhang introduced an invariant of an admissible conformal class and a smooth invariant of the underlying manifold obtained by taking the infimum over all such classes. We use a normalization in which both invariants, denoted by $\beta(M,c)$ and $\beta(M)$, take values in $[0,1)$. We prove that every admissible four-manifold $M$ with $\beta(M)$ sufficiently close to $1/2$ is diffeomorphic to $\mathbb{CP}^2$ up to reversal of orientation. At $\beta(M)=1/2$, this result and the conformal characterization of the Fubini--Study class confirm Conjecture~1.1 of Chang, Gursky, and Zhang. Among admissible four-manifolds with indefinite intersection form, we prove the corresponding stability of the diffeomorphism type of $S^2\times S^2$ near $2/3$. For the one- and two-point blow-ups of $\mathbb{CP}^2$, we show that $\beta(M)$ lies strictly above the respective topological lower bounds of $2/3$ and $23/30$. These results lead us to ask whether $1$ is the only accumulation point of the values of $\beta(M)$ and whether, among simply connected admissible four-manifolds, $\beta(M)$ determines the diffeomorphism type up to reversal of orientation.
item.dc:creator: Mijia Lai

item.title: On the Geometry of Quadratic Maps
item.description: arXiv:2611.30837v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: To analyse a homogeneous quadratic map $Q:\mathbb{R}^k\to\mathbb{R}^\ell$, the critical value variety $\Sigma_{Q}$ of its restriction to the unit sphere is very useful but difficult to handle. We prove its dual hypersurface $\mathcal{F}_{Q}$ is of degree $k$ (providing its equation) and is $\mathit{hyperbolic}$: every line though the origin in $\mathbb{R}^\ell$ cuts it at $k$ real points, counting multiplicities. These facts imply: $\boldsymbol{1}$. $\mathcal{F}_{Q}$ is the union of $k/2$ nested topological hyperspheres if $k$ is even, or the union of $(k-1)/2$ nested topological hyperspheres and one topological projective hyperplane if $k$ is odd. $\boldsymbol{2}$. The Toeplitz-Haussdorf Theorem on the range of of the restriction of $Q$ to the unit sphere if $k>\ell$. $\boldsymbol{3}$. The dual version of the hyperbolicity of $\mathcal{F}_{Q}$ is: the critical value variety $\Sigma_{Q}$ is of class $k$. $\boldsymbol{4}$. For generic $Q:\mathbb{R}^k\to\mathbb{R}^k$, $\Sigma_{Q}$ contains $\lfloor\frac{k-1}{2}\rfloor$ collections of ellipsoids of codimension $2$ consisting of degenerate parabolic points. $\boldsymbol{5}$. If $k>\ell$, the parabolic set in $\Sigma_{Q}$ (if any) is a union of hyperplane closed discs bounded by ellipsoids. $\boldsymbol{6}$. The above ellipsoids (items $4$ and $5$) are in bijection with the isolated singular points in $\mathcal{F}_{Q}$.
item.dc:creator: Ricardo Uribe-Vargas

item.title: Sharp signature-weighted total-curvature bounds for complete minimal submanifolds
item.description: arXiv:2611.30857v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $i:M^n\to\R^{n+p}$ be a complete connected minimal immersion, with $n\ge3$. We get a sharp bound of $\int_M |A|^n\dd\mu$ from below in terms of the number of ends and the mod-two Betti numbers of $M$. As an application, if $\int_M |A|^n\dd\mu<\gamma_n$, then $i(M)$ is an affine $n$-plane. Moreover, if $\int_M |A|^n\dd\mu=\gamma_n$, then $i(M)$ is an $n$-catenoid in an affine $(n+1)$-plane, where $\gamma_n=\frac{[n(n-1)]^{n/2}}{n-1}\Vol(\Sn^n)$.
item.dc:creator: Jiuru Zhou

item.title: Higher-Order Minkowski Inequalities via Gradient-Weighted Hessian Potentials
item.description: arXiv:2611.30919v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a sharp boundary inequality for exterior potentials of a gradient-weighted $k$-Hessian equation under regularity, level-curvature, flux conservation, and radial decay hypotheses. The inequality bounds a power of the Newton flux by the normalized integral of $H_k^p/H_{k-1}^{p-1}$, and equality characterizes balls. After a conformal change of metric, two Newton-tensor divergence identities give comparisons between regular levels even when the slab between them contains critical points. For smooth strictly star-shaped domains with strictly $k$-convex boundary, a companion existence theorem supplies exterior potentials for $p$ close to one. We identify the limiting flux with the integral of $H_{k-1}$ and recover the sharp consecutive Minkowski inequality, including its equality case.
item.dc:creator: Yi Wang, Shuhan Yang

item.title: Codimension two complements in hyperbolic products
item.description: arXiv:2611.30926v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $M$ be a finite-volume locally symmetric manifold modeled on $\H^m \times \H^n$, and let $S$ be a compact, totally geodesic, codimension two submanifold of $M$ modeled on $\H^{m-1} \times \H^{n-1}$. In this paper, we initiate the study of manifolds of the form $N = M \setminus S$. In the case where $M$ is a product and $S$ is connected, we prove that such $N$ admit complete, finite-volume, $A$-regular metrics with non-positive sectional curvature. We also deduce some topological properties of $N$, and algebraic properties of $\pi_1(N)$. In the case where $M$ is irreducible, we show that $N$ admits {\it almost non-positive curvature}. Similar results hold for manifolds $X_d$, which are $d$-fold branched covers of $M$ ramified over $S$. Along the way, we show that there are infinitely many commensurability classes of such pairs $(M,S)$, and develop general curvature formulas for doubly warped product metrics, which may be of independent interest.
item.dc:creator: Hyeran Cho, Jean-Fran\c{c}ois Lafont, Nicholas Miller, Barry Minemyer

item.title: Global $C^{2,\alpha}$ Estimates for Complex $k$-Hessian Equations on K\"ahler Manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2611.30954v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove an a priori $C^{2,\alpha}$ estimate for classical admissible solutions of the complex $k$-Hessian equation on a compact K\"ahler manifold with a positive $C^\alpha$ right-hand side.
item.dc:creator: Yulun Xu

item.title: Surfaces of constant sectional curvature in Minkowski space with a canonical semi-symmetric connection
item.description: arXiv:2611.31006v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study surfaces in Minkowski space $\mathbb{R}^3_1$ with constant intrinsic sectional curvature with respect to canonical semi-symmetric connections, metric or non-metric, determined by a parallel vector field $\mathcal{V}$. We compute the ambient sectional curvature and obtain a formula for the intrinsic sectional curvature of nondegenerate surfaces in terms of their Gauss and mean curvatures. We provide a complete classification of cylindrical surfaces with constant intrinsic sectional curvature, covering all causal characters of $\mathcal{V}$ and of the rulings. For rotational surfaces whose axes are parallel to $\mathcal{V}$, we reduce the constant-curvature condition to an ordinary differential equation. Explicit solutions are obtained for null axes and, in the metric case, for surfaces with zero intrinsic sectional curvature.
item.dc:creator: Muhittin Evren Ayd{\i}n, Rafael L\'opez

item.title: The Kao-Lai-Osting Conjecture for the Second Laplace Eigenvalue on Riemannian Two-Tori
item.description: arXiv:2611.31024v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove the $k=2$ case of the Kao-Lai-Osting conjecture for the area-normalized Laplace spectrum of Riemannian two-tori: $\sup_g \lambda_2(T^2,g)\,\mathrm{Area}(T^2,g) = 8\pi^2/\sqrt{3} + 8\pi$, where the supremum is taken over smooth Riemannian metrics. No smooth metric attains this value. It is approached by a sequence in the equilateral conformal class developing a round spherical bubble, and the equilateral class is the only conformal class whose conformal supremum equals the global one. The upper bound follows from spherical folding and a sharp truncated conformal-area inequality for fundamental embeddings into $S^5$. Normal-curvature and normal-chord estimates yield high-cap area control, with exact elementary estimates on nested high-centre strips. The proof is partly computer-assisted. Rational polynomial inequalities handle the low-weight cap range and the entire residual high-cap region, the latter through exact Bernstein certificates on rational boxes, which are also checked independently in ball arithmetic. The residual product inequality is established by rigorous upper quadratures, with two independent reproducible certificates, in ball and in interval arithmetic, and exact domain-coverage checks.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Pigazzini

item.title: Total curvature and area growth of entire minimal graphs in Heisenberg space
item.description: arXiv:2611.31046v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that entire minimal graphs in Heisenberg space $\mathrm{Nil}_3(\tau)$ have infinite total curvature. Since their Gauss curvature is negative, this means that their intrinsic area growth is not quadratic, as conjectured by P\'erez, Rodr\'iguez and the author. It follows that vertical planes are the only orientable complete stable surfaces with constant mean curvature and quadratic area growth in $\mathrm{Nil}_3(\tau)$, and this classification is extended to surfaces with critical and supercritical constant mean curvature in the homogeneous spaces $\mathbb{E}(\kappa,\tau)$. We also prove that the height of an entire minimal graph in $\mathrm{Nil}_3(\tau)$ grows at most quadratically, as conjectured by Nelli and the author, whence the extrinsic and cylindrical area growths of such a graph are exactly cubic. Our arguments rely on the conformal Calabi-Lee duality between minimal graphs in $\mathrm{Nil}_3(\tau)$ and spacelike graphs with constant mean curvature $\tau$ in the Lorentz-Minkowski space $\mathbb{L}^3$, for which we also get sharp gradient estimates.
item.dc:creator: Jos\'e M. Manzano

item.title: On the stress-bienergy tensor of conformal immersions and hypersurfaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.31059v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the stress-bienergy tensor $\bar S_2$ of a conformal immersion $\phi:(M^m,\bar g)\to(N^n,h)$ with conformal factor $\lambda$, and we compute it, together with its trace and its divergence, in terms of $\lambda$ and of the second fundamental form of the associated isometric immersion. This gives a characterization of biconservative conformal immersions and, for hypersurfaces, we prove that $\mathrm{div}\,\bar S_2=0$ if and only if the tangent part of the bitension field vanishes. We introduce conformally biconservative hypersurfaces and show that a totally umbilical hypersurface of a space form is conformally biconservative with a non-constant conformal factor if and only if this factor is an isoparametric function satisfying an explicit ordinary differential equation. We illustrate this result with several examples, in which dimension four plays a special role. Finally, we study the equation $\bar S_2=0$: on a compact manifold of dimension $m\neq 4$, it forces the associated isometric immersion to be harmonic.
item.dc:creator: Ahmed Mohammed Cherif

item.title: Uniqueness of the Bryant Soliton via the Positive Mass Theorem
item.description: arXiv:2611.31081v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For all $n\ge 4$, we prove that every $n$-dimensional complete noncompact steady gradient Ricci soliton asymptotic to the cylinder $\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{S}^{n-1}$ is, up to scaling, isometric to the Bryant soliton. Our proof combines the exponential Bryant asymptotics of Bamler-Lai with the positive mass theorem in all dimensions through a scalar curvature comparison.
item.dc:creator: Pak-Yeung Chan, Yi Lai

item.title: Harmonic functions near isolated subanalytic singularities: generalized horns and regular blow-up
item.description: arXiv:2611.31091v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $X\subset\mathbb{R}^N$ be a subanalytic set of dimension $d\ge 2$, closed near $0$, with an isolated singularity at $0$ and connected link, whose regular part carries the induced Riemannian metric. We study harmonic functions on $X\setminus\{0\}$ near $0$. (i) If $X$ is bi-Lipschitz equivalent, for the intrinsic metric, to a generalized horn $\{(z^\gamma y,z):\ y\in L,\ z\ge 0\}$, with $\gamma\ge 1$ rational and $L$ compact, connected, subanalytic and analytic, then: - every bounded harmonic function extends continuously to $0$; - every positive harmonic function near $0$ can be written as $qG_X+u_b$, with $q\ge 0$, $u_b$ bounded and $G_X$ a fixed singular profile; - a B\^ocher-type theorem holds: a positive harmonic function is either bounded or tends to $+\infty$, and two divergent ones have a nontrivial linear combination that extends continuously. The proof relies on a volume doubling and weak Poincar\'e condition on intrinsic balls away from $0$, invariant under bi-Lipschitz homeomorphisms, which together with an annular connectedness condition implies a Harnack inequality on annuli; the decomposition then follows from a Picard-principle argument whose geometric input is the Harnack inequality on the links. (ii) If $d\ge 3$ and the spherical blow-up of $X$ at $0$ is a regular manifold with boundary parametrizing $X$ near $0$ (condition (R) of the paper), the singular profile has a polyhomogeneous expansion, which is described and may contain a $\log\rho$ term, $\rho=|x|$. (iii) For the rotational cusps $|x|^2=z^m$, $m>2$, $d\ge 3$, whose spherical blow-up is not regular, the profile is radial of order $\rho^{1-m(d-1)/2}$, so that its exponent depends on the rate at which the sections shrink.
item.dc:creator: Flavio Mosca

item.title: An Elasticity Complex for Kirchhoff--Love Shells
item.description: arXiv:2611.28480v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop an elasticity complex for Kirchhoff--Love shell theory, based on the linearized Gauss--Codazzi equations as compatibility conditions for shell strains. The resulting shell complex forms a fine resolution of the sheaf of infinitesimal rigid motions, so its cohomology groups are determined by the corresponding sheaf cohomology. Remarkably, the complex also reveals an Airy potential representation of equilibrium stress fields. The framework further identifies natural boundary conditions for both kinematic and dynamic variables. Finally, we establish a Hodge--Morrey--Friedrichs decomposition for strain and stress fields on shells with boundary.
item.dc:creator: Hang Yin, Albert Chern

item.title: Finsler--Sobolev inequalities: optimality & rigidity
item.description: arXiv:2611.28624v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish optimal Sobolev and logarithmic-Sobolev inequalities on non-compact, possibly non-reversible Finsler manifolds with non-negative weighted Ricci curvature. The optimal constants exhibit no dependence on reversibility -- confirming Ohta's conjectural principle -- being governed solely by the forward and backward asymptotic volume ratios. We then apply the logarithmic-Sobolev inequality to establish the optimal hypercontractivity estimate for the heat flow in the same geometric setting. The equality cases of the above optimal inequalities imply strong rigidity in the underlying manifold, characterized by fine properties of the flag and $S$-curvatures as well as the precise profiles of the corresponding extremizers. We illustrate our results by examples including Randers metrics obtained by Zermelo navigation with Killing vector fields, and weighted convex cones in $\mathbb{R}^n$ endowed with arbitrary Minkowski norms, the latter showing that the forward and backward asymptotic volume ratios may differ.
item.dc:creator: Alexandru Krist\'aly

item.title: Anti-de Sitter charges and maximal Cauchy hypersurfaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.28989v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct conserved charges of asymptotic symmetries for negative-cosmological-constant vacuum spacetimes from the Neumann data for the Hamiltonian and momentum constraints on maximal conformally-compact Cauchy hypersurfaces. This gives a general and canonical initial value treatment of charges for vacuum spacetimes with timelike conformal boundary.
item.dc:creator: A. Rod Gover, Jaros\l aw Kopi\'nski, Andrew Waldron

item.title: Spin-geodesic systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.29005v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce and study a class of geometric dynamical systems on Riemannian manifolds called spin-geodesic systems, in which the motion of a point is coupled to an internal classical spin through a symmetric endomorphism field $B$, the spin-coupling field. These systems may be viewed as $B$-dependent deformations of geodesic motion and have connections with frame flows, magnetic geodesic flows, and nonholonomic rolling systems. We show that every spin-geodesic system admits an equivalent interpretation as a no-slip rolling system in an abstract ambient geometry; when the associated metric connection, determined by $B$, is flat, this construction reduces, under the usual integrability hypotheses, to ordinary rolling on a Euclidean hypersurface. Our second main result is a Liouville theorem: for an arbitrary symmetric spin-coupling field B, the spin-geodesic flow preserves the canonical Liouville volume on its mechanical phase space. This holds even though the flow is not symplectic unless $B$ is identically zero.
item.dc:creator: Renato Feres, Zijie Hu

item.title: Plane Curves Whose Curvature Is a Function of the Distance to the Tangent Line: Relations Between Karpenkov's Areal and Angular Densities
item.description: arXiv:2611.29065v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For a plane curve and a point $O$, O. Karpenkov introduced the areal density $A$ and the angular density $B$ as smooth counterparts of the alternating entries of an LLS sequence. Here $A$ is the signed distance from $O$ to the tangent line, and, with the order of the chords in the signed definition fixed here, $A^2B=\kappa$, where $\kappa$ is the signed curvature. A relation between the two densities therefore prescribes the curvature as a function of the distance to the tangent line. Karpenkov asked which curves have $AB$, or $B$ alone, constant. The equation $AB=C$ gives the shrinking, stationary and expanding profiles of planar curve shortening. For constant nonzero $B$, choose the orientation so that $B>0$. Curves with positive support have periodic support or are centred circles. The noncircular closed curves are classified by their turning fractions in $(1/2,1/\sqrt3)$; the centred circle is the only embedded closed solution. Negative support gives smooth open graphs whose two ends approach rays from the origin. On positive support the polar reciprocal is a constant-force orbit, and the original curve is a rotated and scaled velocity curve of that orbit. For $A^3B=C$ we determine which ends extend to infinity, reach a cusp, or spiral into the origin. We describe regularity and the range of turning fractions for the positive-support family $A^pB=C$. Finally, for a general relation $B=\Phi(A)$ the polar reciprocal is an orbit of the central force $L^2/\Phi(1/r)$; we describe the ends of all arcs with $AB<0$ and show that a closed curve with turning fraction $m/n$ has exactly $n(m-1)$ double points. We also describe the curves whose areal or angular density is a linear function of the arclength.
item.dc:creator: Esther Notik

item.title: Semiclassical Weyl laws and noncommutative geometry on open manifolds with conformally cusp metrics
item.description: arXiv:2611.29139v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish semiclassical Weyl laws on open Riemannian manifolds with conformally cusp metrics of finite volume. These metrics need not be complete, and even when complete they do not have bounded geometry. Moreover, the potentials are bounded, the discreteness of the spectrum being a consequence of the geometry rather than of a confining potential. Therefore, our results lie beyond the scope of recent semiclassical Weyl laws of Dai--Yan and Braverman. The semiclassical Weyl laws are established for fractional Schr\"odinger operators associated with Dirac operators, magnetic Laplacians, and Hodge Laplacians, under conditions of Moroianu and Gol\'enia--Moroianu which ensure that these operators have discrete spectra. We also obtain extensions of Connes' integration formula for the same operators. In addition, we deal with a class of conformally cusp metrics of infinite volume, in which case the semiclassical Weyl laws and the integration formulas only involve the values at infinity. The results are obtained by applying the abstract semiclassical Weyl laws and integration formulas for spectral triples established in a previous paper.
item.dc:creator: Raphael Ponge

item.title: Sixth-Order Q-Curvature of Conformally Euclidean Metrics: Improved Dimensional Thresholds, Quantitative Lower Bounds and Applications
item.description: arXiv:2611.29534v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper studies the sign of the sixth-order \(Q\)-curvature of conformally Euclidean metrics on \(\mathbb{R}^n\) for integers \(n\ge2m\) and \(m\ge4\). Under suitable assumptions, we refine the sixfold integral estimates and prove that \(Q_g^{(6)}>0\) whenever \(2m\le n\le4m-6+[\widehat h_m]\), where \(\widehat h_m\) is the unique positive root of \(G_m\) and \(\widehat h_m\sim\frac{2\sqrt7-4}{3}m\) as \(m\to\infty\). Moreover, we strengthen this positivity result by establishing the quantitative lower bound \(Q_g^{(6)}(x)\ge\Theta_{m,n}\bigl(Q_g^{(2)}(x)\bigr)^3>0\) for every \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), where \(\Theta_{m,n}>0\) is an explicit constant depending only on \(m\) and \(n\). These quantitative inequalities also yield explicit lower bounds for intermediate Laplacians in higher-order elliptic equations. On the non-positivity side, we construct metrics satisfying \(Q_g^{(6)}(0)<0\) whenever \(n>\widetilde N_m\), where \(\widetilde N_m\sim\widetilde\Lambda m\) as \(m\to\infty\) and \(\widetilde\Lambda\simeq9.74268\). These metrics extend smoothly to \(\mathbb S^n\) and are conformal to the round metric. In the same dimensional range, we further construct metrics with \(Q_g^{(6)}(0)>0\) and establish uniform positive lower and upper bounds for \(Q_g^{(2m)}\) on \(\mathbb R^n\). Our results extend the positivity range and lower the counterexample threshold obtained by V\'etois and Zeitler (arXiv preprint, 2026). The sixth-order estimate also answers a question raised in our previous work on quantitative fourth-order \(Q\)-curvature bounds. These results provide new insights into Conjecture 1 of Li and Xu (J. Funct. Anal. 289 (2025), 111011) in the case \(k=3\), clarifying its validity and limitations across different dimensions.
item.dc:creator: Jianlun Liu, Hong-Rui Sun, Ziheng Zhang

item.title: Symplectizing stable generalized complex four-manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2611.29572v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We explicitly describe a surgery that turns a stable generalized complex four-manifold into a symplectic four-manifold. As a consequence, we show that for $n\geq 2$, the almost complex manifold $(n^2+n+1)S^1\times S^3\#\overline{\mathbb{C}P^2}$ admits no stable generalized complex structures or constant type generalized complex structures. We also prove an irreducibility result for stable generalized complex four-manifolds and we show that the moduli space of generalized complex structures on an elliptic surface has infinitely many components.
item.dc:creator: Gil R. Cavalcanti, Bas Wensink

item.title: Hilbert measures of non-coregular representations of the circle and orthogonal groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.29620v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give explicit constructions of the Hilbert measure, which transports the integral of an invariant smooth function from a representation to the image of the Hilbert embedding, for certain representations of the circle, orthogonal, and special orthogonal groups that are non-coregular, meaning that the algebra of invariants is not a polynomial algebra. These include all $4$-dimension real circle representations, a family of $6$-dimensional circle representations, and $k$ copies of the defining representations of the orthogonal and special orthogonal groups when $k$ is large enough that the representation is not coregular. For the circle representations, we also construct the Hilbert measure on the singular symplectic quotient at level zero.
item.dc:creator: Luca Liebow, Belle Roberge, Christopher Seaton

item.title: On deformations of foliated complex analytic structures IV-2: Obstructed and unobstructed foliated deformations
item.description: arXiv:2611.30317v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study foliated deformations of compact complex manifolds with dimension 1-foliations and codimension 1-foliations, and unfoldings of compact complex manifolds with codimension 1-foliations in terms of deformations of sections with classical examples in deformation theory of complex structures.
item.dc:creator: Chunghoon Kim

item.title: Irreducible shallow tanh neural networks are a manifold
item.description: arXiv:2611.30553v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Neural networks (NNs) have been increasingly used as function approximators, motivating the study of the geometry of their function spaces. We study the set of functions represented by shallow neural networks with hyperbolic tangent activation, fixed input and output dimensions, and $n$ hidden neurons. In particular, we prove that the subset represented by irreducible networks in the sense of Sussmann (Neural Networks, 1992), i.e., networks with no redundant neurons, is a smooth embedded submanifold of the Sobolev spaces $\mathrm{W}^{\ell,p}$ on bounded sets for any $\ell\in\mathbb{N}$ and $p\in[1,+\infty]$. The key step is to show that if a sequence of networks converges in $\mathrm{W}^{\ell,p}$ to an irreducible network with the same number of hidden neurons, then the parameters of the approximating networks remain bounded. Finally, we show that this manifold has exactly $n+1$ connected components when both the input and output are scalar, and is connected otherwise.
item.dc:creator: Ivan Bioli, Isabella Carla Gonnella, Carlo Marcati, Federico Pichi

item.title: The Boundary Conjecture for Smoothable Alexandrov Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.30860v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that in a noncollapsed limit of complete Riemannian manifolds with $\sec\ge\kappa$, each boundary component of a compact full-dimensional convex body, equipped with its intrinsic length metric, has Alexandrov curvature at least $\kappa$. We also consider such a body in the limit of a noncollapsed sequence of Alexandrov spaces with curvature at least $\kappa$. If $\kappa>0$ or the boundary of the body is strongly convex, we show that the body can be approximated by convex bodies in the given sequence.
item.dc:creator: Nina Lebedeva

item.title: Smooth Exterior Potentials for a Gradient-Weighted Hessian Equation
item.description: arXiv:2611.30948v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct a positive solution of an exterior Dirichlet problem for a gradient-weighted $k$-Hessian operator on each smooth strictly star-shaped domain whose boundary curvatures lie in $\Gamma_k$. For $p>1$ sufficiently close to one, the solution is smooth up to the boundary, has no critical points, and is unique among continuous potentials on the natural viscosity branch. Its levels remain strictly star-shaped and strictly $k$-convex. We determine its radial asymptotics through two derivatives and the uniform limit of $(p-1)|Du_p|$ on the boundary. The construction perturbs an inverse curvature-quotient flow. In logarithmic radial coordinates the exact equation is elliptic for $p>1$ and its limit is parabolic. A weighted inverse estimate on the half-cylinder controls the singular perturbation.
item.dc:creator: Yi Wang, Shuhan Yang

item.title: $C^{m,\alpha}$-rectifiability in Carnot groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.30960v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In an arbitrary Carnot group $\mathbb{G}$ of homogeneous dimension $Q$, we characterize rectifiability of sets of finite Hausdorff measure by $\mathbf C_{\mathbb{G}}^{m,\alpha}$-regular surfaces with complemented vertical tangent subgroups, for every $m\ge1$ and $\alpha\in[0,1]$. The criterion combines positive lower density with approximation in measure by tubes around such surfaces. At almost every point, one tube radius $\lambda r^{m+\alpha}$ suffices for $\alpha>0$, whereas the estimate must hold for every $\lambda r^m$, $\lambda>0$, for $\alpha=0$. Tubular approximation upgrades $\mathbf C^1_{\mathbb{G}}$-rectifiability to class $(m,\alpha)$ without an additional density assumption. The proof combines ambient normal-form polynomial jets, a Remez-type norming inequality, and Whitney extension. In topological dimension at least two, quantitative volume approximation by noncharacteristic sublevel sets yields higher-order rectifiability of reduced boundaries. In particular, for weak solutions of the horizontal Poisson equation with $L^q_{\mathrm{loc}}$ forcing ($q>\max\{Q,2\}$ finite), almost every sublevel set has second-order rectifiable reduced boundary.
item.dc:creator: Kennedy Obinna Idu, Francesco Paolo Maiale

item.title: Connected Lie groups with a left-invariant intrinsic chronometer
item.description: arXiv:2611.30995v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we investigate left-invariant intrinsic chronometers (time functions) on connected finite-dimensional Lie groups. We formulate and prove sub-Lorentzian analogs of V.\,N.\,Berestovskii's classical direct and inverse theorems. A one-to-one correspondence is established between chronometers satisfying the proposed system of axioms (including upper semi-continuity and the condition that the interiors of chronological rhombi form a base for the topology) and smooth left-invariant sub-Lorentzian structures. It is shown that an axiomatic chronometer uniquely determines a closed, pointed, convex cone in the Lie algebra, whose linear span satisfies the Chow--Rashevskii condition, and an upper semi-continuous concave positively homogeneous anti-norm on it. Conversely, it is proved that any such algebraic structure satisfying a local chronologicity condition induces an intrinsic chronometer with the required properties. The proofs rely on local estimates in exponential coordinates, the Hahn--Banach separation theorem, and properties of weak limits in optimal control problems.
item.dc:creator: Ramazan G. Beden

item.title: Isoparametric functions on Finsler space forms
item.description: arXiv:2212.07625v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we prove that each connected regular level hypersurface of a transnormal function on a Finsler space form $(N(c),F)$ has constant principal curvatures under suitable conditions. This result extends Miyaoka's refinement of Q. M. Wang's classical theorem on transnormal functions in Riemannian space forms to the Finsler setting. On forward Finsler space forms $(\overrightarrow{N}(c),F)$, we discuss the relationship between umbilic hypersurfaces and isoparametric hypersurfaces, and construct global and local isoparametric functions using the distance function.
item.dc:creator: Yali Chen, Qun He

item.title: The complete dynamics description of positively curved metrics in the Wallach flag manifold $\mathrm{SU}(3)/\mathrm{T}^2$
item.description: arXiv:2307.06418v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The family of invariant Riemannian manifolds in the Wallach flag manifold $\mathrm{SU}(3)/\mathrm{T}^2$ is described by three parameters $(x,y,z)$ of positive real numbers. By restricting such a family of metrics in the \emph{tetrahedron} $\cal{T}:= x+y+z = 1$, in this paper, we describe all regions $\cal R \subset \cal T$ admitting metrics with curvature properties varying from positive sectional curvature to positive scalar curvature, including positive intermediate curvature notion's. We study the dynamics of such regions under the \emph{projected Ricci flow} in the plane $(x,y)$, concluding sign curvature maintenance and escaping. In addition, we obtain some results for positive intermediate Ricci curvature for a path of metrics on fiber bundles over $\mathrm{SU}(3)/\mathrm{T}^2$, further studying its evolution under the Ricci flow on the base.
item.dc:creator: Leonardo F. Cavenaghi, Lino Grama, Ricardo M. Martins, Douglas D. Novaes

item.title: Metric-Measure Concentration and Strong Cosmic Censorship in Vacuum Gowdy Spacetimes
item.description: arXiv:2308.00080v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that a smooth vacuum $T^3$-Gowdy maximal globally hyperbolic development is $C^2$-inextendible if its asymptotic velocity differs from one on a dense subset of the singular circle. This is the implication posed in Section~14.2 of Ringstr\"om's 2010 review. The proof compares the spacetime volume of a timelike boundary collar with that of a shrinking angular cone, using Killing transport and the Einstein constraint. We connect this criterion to Gromov's observable distance: the physical spatial mm-spaces satisfy the lower bound $d_{\rm conc}(X_\tau,*)\ge L(\tau)/(4+L(\tau))$, where $L(\tau)$ is the length of the orbit circle. If $L(\tau)\to0$, then $v_\infty\ge1$ everywhere, the critical set $\{v_\infty=1\}$ has Lebesgue measure zero, and the development is $C^2$-inextendible. Thus physical point concentration is sufficient for inextendibility, but is not necessary. We also give explicit, non-perturbative subcritical characteristic conditions on vacuum Cauchy data ensuring quantitative Kretschmann blow-up without using Gowdy asymptotic theorems in the curvature estimate. The exact volume-transfer identity yields predictive monotonicity criteria and distinguishes coordinate localization from intrinsic metric collapse. In the transversely expanding regime, observable rescalings with an extended transverse-length limit are classified as a point, a measured circle, or the maximal pyramid; a uniform spectral estimate eliminates all nontrivial toroidal Fourier sectors, including in the presence of spikes. The geometric framework is completed by quantitative tube estimates, a local CMC redistribution theorem, and constrained variational descriptions of the reduced energy current and normalized-volume flow.
item.dc:creator: S. L. Cacciatori, P. Ursino

item.title: The universal Euler characteristic and Burnside group for definable groupoids
item.description: arXiv:2310.12073v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce the universal Euler characteristic of orbit space definable groupoids, a class of groupoids containing cocompact proper Lie groupoids as well as translation groupoids associated to proper definable group actions. We show that every additive and multiplicative invariant of orbit space definable groupoids with an additional local triviality hypothesis arises as a ring homomorphism applied to the universal Euler characteristic. This in particular includes the $\Gamma$-orbifold Euler characteristic introduced by the first and third authors when $\Gamma$ is a finitely presented group. For definable groupoids, where the object and arrow spaces as well as the structure maps are definable, we also introduce a Burnside group which is an analog of the classical Burnside ring associated to compact Lie groups and, for a transitive groupoid with compact isotropy, admits a partial multiplication.
item.dc:creator: Carla Farsi, Emily Proctor, Christopher Seaton

item.title: Examples of Ricci limit spaces with infinite holes
item.description: arXiv:2404.00619v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $n\geq 3$, $\lambda \in \mathbb{R} $, and $(X,h)$ be an $n$-dimensional smooth complete Riemannian manifold with ${\rm Ric}_h > \lambda $. In this paper, we construct, for each given $\epsilon >0$, a sequence of $(n+2)$-dimensional manifolds $(M_{i} ,g_i ) \stackrel{GH}{\longrightarrow} (X_\epsilon ,d_\epsilon ) $ with ${\rm Ric}_{g_i} > \lambda $, such that $d_{GH} (X,X_\epsilon ) \leq \epsilon $, and $X_\epsilon $ is homeomorphic to the space obtained by removing an infinite number of balls from $X$. Hence $X_\epsilon $ has dense boundary with an infinite number of connected components. Moreover, $X_\epsilon $ has no open subset which is topologically a manifold. This generalizes Hupp-Naber-Wang's result (arxiv: 2308.03909) from $4$-dimensional case to the general case of dimension $n\geq 3$. Our construction differs from that of Hupp-Naber-Wang. In their approach, Hupp-Naber-Wang considered doing an infinite number of blow-ups on the local complex surface structure of $X$, thus relying on the $4$-dimensional condition.
